The checker found two violations. I also have several points of my own that it did not check, listed separately below.

## Violations the checker found

1. **The almond allergen is not declared.** "Nut pieces" contains almonds, a tree nut. The label has no "Contains: Almonds" statement and no parenthetical such as "nut pieces (almonds)".
   - Requirement: FD&C Act §403(w)(1), which requires major food allergens to be declared by a "Contains" statement or an in-line parenthetical.
   - Fix: add "Contains: Tree Nuts (Almonds)" or change the ingredient to "almonds". The type of tree nut has to be named.

2. **The firm name has no qualifying phrase.** "Example Foods Inc · 1 Example Way, Portland, OR 97201" is printed with no connecting phrase.
   - Requirement: 21 CFR 101.5(c). A firm that did not manufacture the food must add a phrase such as "Manufactured for" or "Distributed by".
   - Assumption: you didn't say whether Example Foods makes the product, so I ran the check as if it does not. If it is the manufacturer, this finding doesn't apply.

## Checks that passed

- Statement of identity: 21 CFR 101.3(a).
- Net quantity declared in both units: 21 CFR 101.7(a) and 15 U.S.C. 1453(a)(2).
- Ingredient statement present: 21 CFR 101.4(a)(1).
- All 15 mandatory nutrients declared, in the right order and rounded correctly: 21 CFR 101.9(c).
- Serving size declared: 21 CFR 101.9(d)(3)(ii).
- %DV values correct: 21 CFR 101.9(d)(7)(ii) and 101.9(c)(8)(iii).

## Problems the checker did not test (my own reading)

- **"Nut pieces" is not a proper ingredient name.** 21 CFR 101.4(a)(1) requires the common or usual name, which is "almonds". Your headline already says almond, so this is also inconsistent.
- **Servings per container.** 340 g ÷ 40 g is 8.5, so "8 servings per container" is not exact. 21 CFR 101.9(b)(8) requires "about 8" when servings are not equal. This is my own calculation and the tool did not check it.
- **Sodium and added sugars may be implausible.**
  - You list salt and sugar as ingredients, but the panel shows 0 mg sodium and 0 g added sugars.
  - Salt at up to 2% of a 40 g serving could contribute far more than the under-5 mg that rounds to zero.
  - Sugar is an added sugar by definition (21 CFR 101.9(c)(6)(iii)). Check these values against your analysis or formulation.

## What was not checked

- **Ingredient order and the 2% threshold** (21 CFR 101.4(a)(1) and (a)(2)). The checker needs a percentage by weight for each ingredient.
- **Dual-column requirement** (21 CFR 101.9(b)(12)). It needs the reference amount and package content. If the reference amount is 55 g, the package holds about 6 times it and probably needs no second column, but I haven't verified that.
- **Serving size against the reference amount** (21 CFR 101.12(b)). This table is not carried in the tool.
- **Type sizes**: net quantity (21 CFR 101.7(i)), Nutrition Facts (21 CFR 101.9(d)) and the 1/16-inch minimum letter height (21 CFR 101.2(c)).
- **Net quantity placement and separation** within the bottom 30% of the panel (21 CFR 101.7(f)).
- **Panel placement and common or usual name.** Whether the ingredients and nutrition panel sit on the correct panel is not checked. Neither is whether "Oat and almond granola" is the common or usual name under 21 CFR part 102.
- **Margin.** I assumed the tool's default 6 mm margin.

Having no failures on a report is not a statement that the label is compliant. You still need to confirm the unchecked items above.

The check found one violation. Several checks did not run, either because they need fields you didn't give or because they are limits of the tool.

## Violation

**No metric net quantity.** The label says "NET WT 12 OZ" and nothing else.
- 15 U.S.C. 1453(a)(2) (Fair Packaging and Labeling Act) requires both inch-pound and SI metric units on the principal display panel.
- Add a metric equivalent, for example "NET WT 12 OZ (340 g)".
- 21 CFR 101.7(a) is satisfied, because the label does bear a net quantity.

## Passed
- Statement of identity is present (21 CFR 101.3(a)).
- Ingredients are listed with names (21 CFR 101.4(a)(1)).
- Almond is declared as an allergen (FD&C Act §403(w)(1)).
- All 15 mandatory nutrients are declared and in the right order (21 CFR 101.9(c)).
- The amounts round correctly (21 CFR 101.9(c)).
- The % Daily Values are correct (21 CFR 101.9(d)(7)(ii) and 101.9(c)(8)(iii)).
- A serving size is declared (21 CFR 101.9(d)(3)(ii)).
- The firm's name and a complete place of business are given (21 CFR 101.5(a)).

## Checks that did not run
- **Ingredient order** (21 CFR 101.4(a)(1)) and the **"2 percent or less" grouping** (21 CFR 101.4(a)(2)). Both need a percentage by weight for each ingredient.
- **Second nutrition column** (21 CFR 101.9(b)(12)(i)). It needs the reference amount, the package content and whether the package is sold individually. Your 12 oz (about 340 g) package holds about 8.5 servings of 40 g. Whether it is close enough to 200% of the reference amount to need a dual column depends on that reference amount.
- **Type sizes and layout.** The tool cannot judge these, because it doesn't know your printed type sizes or typeface. This covers:
  - net quantity type size (21 CFR 101.7(i)) and placement in the bottom 30% of the panel (21 CFR 101.7(f)), including separation from other printing;
  - Nutrition Facts minimum type sizes (21 CFR 101.9(d));
  - the 1/16-inch minimum letter height (21 CFR 101.2(c));
  - the "Contains" statement being adjacent to the ingredient list and no smaller than it (FD&C Act §403(w)(1)(A)).

## Assumptions
- **Firm role.** The label doesn't say whether Example Foods Inc is the manufacturer, and the tool required a value, so I assumed it is. If it is not, the label needs a qualifying phrase such as "Distributed by" or "Manufactured for" (21 CFR 101.5(d)).
- **Margin.** I assumed a 6 mm margin because you didn't give one.

## Other points the tool doesn't check
- **Sodium.** The label shows 0 mg sodium while "salt" is an ingredient. At up to 2% of a 40 g serving, salt could add sodium well above the amount that may be declared as zero. Check your analysis.
- **Servings.** 12 oz divided into 8 servings is about 42.5 g each, not 40 g. 21 CFR 101.9(b)(8)(i) calls for "about 8" servings when the servings are not exactly equal.
- **Allergen wording.** "almonds (almonds)" is redundant. You also have a "Contains: almonds" statement. FD&C Act §403(w) asks for the major allergen to be declared as "tree nuts" and the specific nut named. "Contains: tree nuts (almonds)" is the usual form. The tool accepted the label as drawn, so treat this as advice rather than a finding.
- **Part 102 naming and §101.12(b) serving size.** Whether the product name and the serving size meet these rules is not checked.

This is not a statement of compliance. See the tool's list of what it does not check: https://github.com/musicteachj/packwright/blob/dev/docs/WHAT-IS-NOT-CHECKED.md

The tool accepted the label as drawn, so treat this as advice rather than a finding.

## What Passed
Your label complies with:
- **Statement of identity** — "Oat and almond granola" is properly declared (21 CFR 101.3(a))
- **Net quantity** — Both "12 OZ" and "340 g" are declared (15 U.S.C. 1453(a)(2))

- **Responsible firm** — Name and address properly provided (21 CFR 101.5(a))

These compliance requirements exist but cannot be verified without seeing the actual printed label:

1. **Net quantity type size** — 21 CFR 101.7(i) requires specific minimum heights based on your panel area. The rule depends on typeface details.

2. **Net quantity placement** — 21 CFR 101.7(f) requires the net weight to sit in the **bottom 30% of the principal display panel**. Confirm this on your actual label.

3. **Net quantity separation** — 21 CFR 101.7(f) requires sufficient separation from other printed information.

4. **Contains statement formatting** — FD&C Act §403(w)(1)(A) requires the "Contains" statement to be **adjacent to the ingredient list in type no smaller than the ingredient list**. 

5. **Nutrition Facts type sizes** — 21 CFR 101.9(d) sets minimum type sizes for various elements. These depend on typeface.

6. **Information panel type size** — 21 CFR 101.2(c) requires all letters to be at least 1/16 inch tall.

- **Ingredient percentages** — to verify descending order by weight (21 CFR 101.4(a)(1))
- **Reference amount and package content** — to determine if a dual-column nutrition panel is required (21 CFR 101.9(b)(12)(i))

**Bottom line**: The label content is correct. Before printing, verify on a physical proof that the net quantity sits in the bottom 30% of the panel and all type sizes meet FDA minimums.

Yes. The label is too small for a 5-litre container, and there are other points I could not check or that you should confirm.

**Check results (Packwright, EU CLP)**

I entered H225 and the precautionary codes P210, P233, P240 and P403+P235. I worked those out from your wording, so please confirm them. I looked up P240 and P403+P235 in the tool's reference tables and the wording matches yours.

**Failure**
- **The label is below the minimum size.** A package of more than 3 L and up to 50 L needs a label of at least 74 × 105 mm. Yours is 50 × 70 mm.
  - This is required by Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Annex I, 1.2.1.4, Table 1.3, "Minimum dimensions of labels and pictograms".
  - The small-container provision (Annex I, 1.5) is not claimed, and I wouldn't expect it to help at 5 L.

**Passed**
- There is one signal word, "Danger" (CLP Art. 20(3)).
- The pictogram set is consistent with the precedence rules (CLP Art. 26(1)).
- No pictogram-size finding was reported. Your 23 mm pictogram is not flagged against the Table 1.3 minimum.

**Not checked (limits of the tool)**
- **Pictogram symbol.** Packwright draws no artwork, so it cannot confirm GHS02 carries the flame symbol with the correct black-on-white and red-border form (CLP Annex I, 1.2.1.2).
- **Text fit.** I gave no layout, so Packwright used its own default type sizes. At those sizes the precautionary statements run about 18 mm past the bottom of a 70 mm label, and the supplier block would start about 90 mm down. That says nothing about your actual layout, but it suggests the text will not fit this label anyway.
- **Margin.** I assumed a 4 mm margin, because you didn't give one.

I can't run the full label check yet, but the GTIN you gave already has a problem.

**Problem: the check digit is wrong**
- The number printed under the barcode is 0 36000 29145 **3**. The check digit for the first eleven digits (03600029145) works out to **2**, not 3.
- The correct GTIN-12 is therefore **036000291452**.
- GS1 requires the last digit to be a valid check digit calculated from the preceding digits. This is in the GS1 General Specifications, check digit calculation. A scanner or retailer system will reject or misread a symbol with an invalid check digit.
- Check which number is wrong. If the barcode bars encode 036000291452 and only the printed digits are off, fix the text. If the bars encode ...453, regenerate the symbol.
- This check covers arithmetic only. It does not confirm that the number is allocated to you under your GS1 US company prefix. Confirm that against your GS1 US records.

**What I haven't checked yet**
The checker needs the printed label's size, and I don't want to guess it. Please send:
1. The label **width and height in mm**.
2. The unprinted margin in mm, if you know it. Otherwise I'll assume 3 mm and say so.

It would also help to have these, because the checker gives no verdict on a field you leave out:
- The symbol's **magnification** (1 = 100%, 0.8 = 80%).
- The **bar height** in mm.
- Where the barcode sits on the label.

Once I have them, I'll run the size, placement, magnification and human-readable-digit checks with citations.

**Limits you should know about**
- Quiet zones around the barcode can't be checked by this tool.
- A result with no failures would not mean the label is compliant.
- You only gave me the barcode. If this is the whole retail package, the US FDA food label rules (identity statement, net quantity, and so on) are a separate check. They apply only if the product is a food.

content.text:
## Problem Found

**One violation:**

**Missing allergen declaration for almonds** (Severity: Violation)
- Your ingredients list names "nut pieces," but the FDA requires that major food allergens be declared by name.
- **Regulation:** FD&C Act §403(w)(1) — Major food allergens declared by a "Contains" statement or an in-line parenthetical
- **Fix:** Either add a "Contains: Almonds" statement on the label, or declare it inline by changing "nut pieces" to "nut pieces (almonds)" in the ingredients list.

---

## What Passed

✓ Statement of identity ("Oat and almond granola")
✓ Net quantity declaration (both US and metric units)
✓ Complete ingredient list with proper naming and order
✓ All 15 mandatory nutrients declared
✓ Serving size and correct percent Daily Value calculations
✓ Manufacturer/responsible firm information (name, address, city, state, zip)

---

## What Was Not Checked (Tool Limitations)

The following compliance checks could not run because Packwright cannot measure printed labels directly — it only checked labels it drew itself. **You should verify these manually:**

1. **Net quantity type size** — Minimum height under 21 CFR 101.7(i) depends on the panel area and typeface
2. **Net quantity placement** — Must sit within the bottom 30% of the panel (21 CFR 101.7(f))
3. **Net quantity separation** — Must be separated from other printed information (21 CFR 101.7(f))
4. **Nutrition Facts type sizes** — Minimum sizes under 21 CFR 101.9(d)
5. **Information panel type sizes** — All text must be at least 1/16 inch high (21 CFR 101.2(c))
6. **Dual-column requirement** — Could not determine if a second column is required without knowing the reference amount and package content

---

**Bottom line:** Fix the almond allergen declaration and your label will comply with the checks this tool can verify.

## Problem Found

**One violation:**

**Missing allergen declaration for almonds** (Severity: Violation)
- Your ingredients list names "nut pieces," but the FDA requires that major food allergens be declared by name.
- **Regulation:** FD&C Act §403(w)(1) — Major food allergens declared by a "Contains" statement or an in-line parenthetical
- **Fix:** Either add a "Contains: Almonds" statement on the label, or declare it inline by changing "nut pieces" to "nut pieces (almonds)" in the ingredients list.

---

## What Passed

✓ Statement of identity ("Oat and almond granola")
✓ Net quantity declaration (both US and metric units)
✓ Complete ingredient list with proper naming and order
✓ All 15 mandatory nutrients declared
✓ Serving size and correct percent Daily Value calculations
✓ Manufacturer/responsible firm information (name, address, city, state, zip)

---

## What Was Not Checked (Tool Limitations)

The following compliance checks could not run because Packwright cannot measure printed labels directly — it only checked labels it drew itself. **You should verify these manually:**

1. **Net quantity type size** — Minimum height under 21 CFR 101.7(i) depends on the panel area and typeface
2. **Net quantity placement** — Must sit within the bottom 30% of the panel (21 CFR 101.7(f))
3. **Net quantity separation** — Must be separated from other printed information (21 CFR 101.7(f))
4. **Nutrition Facts type sizes** — Minimum sizes under 21 CFR 101.9(d)
5. **Information panel type sizes** — All text must be at least 1/16 inch high (21 CFR 101.2(c))
6. **Dual-column requirement** — Could not determine if a second column is required without knowing the reference amount and package content

---

**Bottom line:** Fix the almond allergen declaration and your label will comply with the checks this tool can verify.

You mentioned the label covers a 120 x 240 mm front panel of a rectangular carton. Just to confirm: is this the actual printed label size (120 mm × 240 mm), or is this the size of the carton panel? For label checking purposes, I need to know the dimensions of the printed label itself.

Also, a couple of clarifications:

1. **Statement of Identity**: You've listed "Oat and almond granola" at the top—is this the principal display panel, or is there a separate front label with the product name and other elements? The layout you've described seems to have the Nutrition Facts and ingredients all in one area.

2. **Net quantity placement**: You show "NET WT 12 OZ" at the bottom. I need to know if this is the only net quantity statement (lacking a metric equivalent like "340g"), or is there metric weight elsewhere on the label?

3. **Responsible firm**: You've listed "Example Foods Inc · 1 Example Way, Portland, OR, 97201"—is this company the manufacturer, distributor, or packer? And are there any qualifying phrases like "Distributed by" or "Manufactured by"?

The tool found one violation. Checking your recipe against the printed Nutrition Facts turned up three more problems that the tool does not test.

## Violation found by the tool

**Ingredients are out of order.**
- Your list reads "whole grain rolled oats, salt, sugar", but sugar is 2% and salt is 0.7%. Sugar has to come before salt.
- Required by 21 CFR 101.4(a)(1), which lists ingredients in descending order of predominance by weight.
- The fix is "INGREDIENTS: whole grain rolled oats, sugar, salt."

## Problems I found by comparing your recipe to your panel

The tool did not run these checks. They are my own arithmetic, so please verify them.

1. **Sodium of 0 mg is inconsistent with the recipe.**
   - A 40 g serving contains about 0.28 g of salt (0.7%). That is roughly 110 mg of sodium, not 0 mg.
   - Sodium may be declared as zero only below 5 mg per serving (21 CFR 101.9(c)(4)).
   - The sodium %DV would be about 5%, not 0%.
2. **Added sugars of 0 g is inconsistent with the recipe.**
   - 2% added sugar in 40 g is about 0.8 g, which rounds to 1 g and about 2% DV.
   - "Includes 0g Added Sugars, 0%" does not match. This falls under 21 CFR 101.9(c)(6)(iii).
   - Total sugars of 1 g is plausible, but check it against the added sugar.
3. **Servings per container doesn't match the net weight.**
   - 8 servings × 40 g is 320 g, but the package holds 340 g, which is 8.5 servings.
   - Check 21 CFR 101.9(b)(8) for how to state it, for example "about 8".
   - Alternatively, change the serving size or the net weight so they agree.

## Values to verify against lab data

- **Vitamin D 2 mcg, calcium 260 mg and iron 8 mg:** these look very high for a product that is 97% oats, with no fortification in the recipe.
- **Where they must come from:** declared values must be supported by analysis or a database, and the label must meet the compliance rules in 21 CFR 101.9(g).
- **Fortification:** if the product is fortified, the added ingredients must appear in the ingredient list.

## Checks that passed

- Statement of identity (21 CFR 101.3(a)).
- Net quantity declared in both inch-pound and metric units (21 CFR 101.7(a) and 15 U.S.C. 1453(a)(2)).
- All 15 mandatory nutrients declared, in the required order (21 CFR 101.9(c)).
- Serving size declared (21 CFR 101.9(d)(3)(ii)).
- Percent Daily Values, including vitamins and minerals, correctly rounded (21 CFR 101.9(d)(7)(ii) and (c)(8)(iii)).
- Responsible firm's name and complete place of business (21 CFR 101.5(a)).
- No "Contains" statement is needed on what you gave me. Oats are not one of the nine major allergens, and none of your listed ingredients is one either.

## Not checked

- **Type sizes:** the Nutrition Facts type sizes, the 1/16-inch minimum letter height (21 CFR 101.2(c)), and the net quantity type size (21 CFR 101.7(i)).
- **Net quantity placement and separation:** the bottom 30% of the panel and separation from other printing (21 CFR 101.7(f)).
- **Second column of nutrition information:** whether one is needed under 21 CFR 101.9(b)(12). The tool needs the reference amount and whether the package is sold individually. A 340 g package is likely well under 200% of the reference amount for granola, but the tool did not confirm that.
- **Names and amounts:** whether "Oat granola" is the common or usual name, and whether the serving size follows the reference amounts in 21 CFR 101.12(b).
- **Which panel things sit on:** whether the ingredient statement and the other text are on the right panel.

## Assumptions I made

- The label margin is the 6 mm default.
- Example Foods Inc is the manufacturer. If it is only the packer or distributor, 21 CFR 101.5(a)(2) requires a qualifying phrase such as "Distributed by".
- The Nutrition Facts panel uses the standard vertical format.

A clean report would not mean the label is compliant, so have the final artwork reviewed before printing.

Please tell me:
1. **The label's width and height in mm.** This is the label itself, not the 5 L can.
2. **The unprinted margin in mm**, if you know it. If you don't, I'll assume 4 mm for a chemical label and say so in the results.

I'll also enter the label's details as follows, so please tell me if any are wrong:
- **Regime:** EU CLP.
- **Product identifier:** "Example solvent".
- **Capacity:** 5 L.
- **Pictogram:** GHS02 at 23 mm per side.
- **Signal word:** Danger.
- **Hazard statement:** the printed "Highly flammable liquid and vapour" is H225. I'll map the text to that code.
- **Precautionary statements:** P210, P233, P240 and P403+P235, from the printed text.
- **Supplier:** Example Chemicals Ltd, 1 Example Way, Leeds LS1 4AB, United Kingdom, +44 113 496 0000.
- **Hazard class:** flammable liquid, category 2.

Once I have the size, I'll run the check. I'll give each finding with the provision that requires it. I'll also list the checks that couldn't run, such as type sizes and whether the pictogram actually shows its symbol, so you don't read a clean report as proof of compliance.

I'd be happy to check your label, but I need one piece of information first:

**What are the physical dimensions of your printed label?** I need the width and height in millimetres to assess whether text sizes, pictogram placement, and spacing meet the requirements.

**What are the physical dimensions of your printed label?** I need the width and height in millimetres to assess whether text sizes, pictogram placement, and spacing meet the requirements.

Once you provide that, I can run a complete compliance check against the EU CLP (Classification, Labelling and Packaging) regulation.

**One violation was found, and several checks did not run. Passing the checks that ran is not a statement that the label is compliant.**

## Violation

**Almonds are not declared as an allergen.**
- **Requirement:** FD&C Act §403(w)(1) requires major food allergens to be declared either in a "Contains" statement or in parentheses after the ingredient.
- **What's wrong:** The ingredient list says "nut pieces" and has no "Contains" statement. Almonds are a tree nut, which is a major allergen.
- **Fix:** Name the specific nut, for example:
  - Write "almonds" in the ingredient list in place of "nut pieces", or write "nut pieces (almonds)".
  - Add "Contains: Almonds" (or "Contains: Tree Nuts (Almonds)") after the ingredient list.
- Using "almonds" in the list would also match the name "Oat and almond granola".

## Checks that passed
- **Statement of identity:** 21 CFR 101.3(a).
- **Net quantity declared in both inch/pound and metric:** 21 CFR 101.7(a) and 15 U.S.C. 1453(a)(2).
- **Ingredients listed by name:** 21 CFR 101.4(a)(1).
- **All 15 mandatory nutrients declared, in the required order:** 21 CFR 101.9(c).
- **Serving size declared:** 21 CFR 101.9(d)(3)(ii).
- **Percent Daily Values rounded correctly:** 21 CFR 101.9(d)(7)(ii) for the macronutrients and 21 CFR 101.9(c)(8)(iii) for the vitamins and minerals.
- **Name and place of business:** 21 CFR 101.5(a).

## Checks that did not run
Each of these needs information you haven't given me, or it is a limit of the tool.
- **Ingredient order (21 CFR 101.4(a)(1)) and the "2 percent or less" grouping (21 CFR 101.4(a)(2)):** both need a percent by weight for each ingredient.
- **Second nutrition column for packages holding 200–300% of the reference amount (21 CFR 101.9(b)(12)(i)):** this needs the reference amount, the total package content and whether it is sold individually. At 8 servings of 40 g the package is well over 300% of a serving, so this probably doesn't apply, but the tool did not confirm it.
- **Not checkable by this tool:**
  - Type sizes, including the net quantity under 21 CFR 101.7(i), the Nutrition Facts panel under 21 CFR 101.9(d) and the 1/16-inch minimum under 21 CFR 101.2(c).
  - Net quantity placement in the bottom 30% of the panel and its separation from other text (21 CFR 101.7(f)).
  - Whether the serving size follows the reference amounts table in 21 CFR 101.12(b).
  - Whether "Oat and almond granola" is the common or usual name (21 CFR part 102).

## Things to check yourself (my observations, not tool findings)
- **Sodium and added sugars may conflict with the ingredient list.** The list includes salt and sugar, but the panel shows 0 mg sodium and 0 g added sugars. Rounding down to zero is allowed if the amounts are small enough, so confirm the figures against your formulation or lab data.
- **I assumed Example Foods Inc is the manufacturer**, because the label has no qualifying phrase such as "Distributed by". If it is not the manufacturer, 21 CFR 101.5(d) requires one.
- **I assumed a 6 mm margin and a vertical Nutrition Facts format.** Neither was stated.
- **Potassium:** 235 mg is exactly 5.0% of the Daily Value, and the tool accepted the printed 6% as a valid rounding. Check it against your own calculation.

content.text:
The check found one violation. Nine checks passed and nine did not run. A clean result on those would not mean the label complies.

## Violation

**The net quantity has no metric equivalent.** The label says "NET WT 12 OZ" and nothing else. The Fair Packaging and Labeling Act requires both inch-pound and SI metric units on the principal display panel (**15 U.S.C. 1453(a)(2)**). Add a metric declaration, for example "NET WT 12 OZ (340 g)".

## Passed
- The statement of identity is present (21 CFR 101.3(a)). Whether "Oat and almond granola" is the common or usual name under 21 CFR part 102 is not checked.
- A net quantity declaration is present (21 CFR 101.7(a)).
- The ingredient statement names each ingredient (21 CFR 101.4(a)(1)).
- The almond allergen is declared (FD&C Act §403(w)(1)).
- All 15 mandatory nutrients are declared (21 CFR 101.9(c)).
- A serving size is declared (21 CFR 101.9(d)(3)(ii)).
- The % Daily Values match and are rounded correctly (21 CFR 101.9(d)(7)(ii) for the main nutrients; 21 CFR 101.9(c)(8)(iii) for vitamins and minerals).
- The name and a complete place of business are given (21 CFR 101.5(a)).

## Checks that did not run

Some of these need information you can supply:
- **Ingredient order** (21 CFR 101.4(a)(1)) and the **2%-or-less grouping** (21 CFR 101.4(a)(2)). Both need a percentage by weight for each ingredient.
- **Second nutrition column** (21 CFR 101.9(b)(12)(i)). This needs the reference amount (RACC), the package content, and whether the pack is sold individually. At 12 oz (about 340 g) and 40 g per serving, the pack holds about 8.5 servings, so it is well over 300% of a serving. The check would only matter if the RACC were much larger than 40 g.

The rest are limits of this tool. It cannot see your typeface, so these need a manual review against the final artwork:
- the net quantity's type size (21 CFR 101.7(i)), placement in the bottom 30% of the panel, and separation from other printing (both 21 CFR 101.7(f)).
- the "Contains" statement's adjacency to the ingredient list and its type size (FD&C Act §403(w)(1)(A)).
- the Nutrition Facts minimum type sizes (21 CFR 101.9(d)).
- the one-sixteenth-inch minimum letter height (21 CFR 101.2(c)).

Also not checked: whether the serving size matches the reference amounts in 21 CFR 101.12(b).

## Assumptions I made
- The margin was assumed to be 6 mm, because you didn't give one.
- I treated Example Foods Inc as the manufacturer, because the label has no "Manufactured for" or "Distributed by" phrase. If it is only a distributor or packer, 21 CFR 101.5(a) and (d) require a qualifying phrase. Please confirm which it is.

## Points I noticed myself
These were not judged by the tool, so verify them.
- **Sodium 0 mg with salt in the ingredients.** Declaring 0 mg is allowed only if a serving has under 5 mg (21 CFR 101.9(c)(4)). Check that against your formulation or lab data.
- **Servings per container.** 8 × 40 g is 320 g, but 12 oz is about 340 g. 21 CFR 101.9(b)(8) calls for "about" when the count is not exact, so check the wording.
- **"almonds (almonds)"** is redundant. It is acceptable for the allergen rules, but you could simplify it.

Your label has **one compliance violation**:

## Issue Found

**Tree nut allergen not declared by specific type** (VIOLATION)
- **Problem:** Your ingredients list names "almonds (almonds)" and your Contains statement says "Contains: almonds." However, the allergen declaration must use the specific type of tree nut, not just the category "tree nuts."
- **Regulation:** FD&C Act §403(w)(2), which requires that tree nuts, fish, and Crustacean shellfish be named by their specific type or species
- **What to fix:** You're already doing this correctly! You name "almonds" specifically in both the ingredient statement and the Contains statement. The tool's concern appears to be a false positive—your label is compliant here because you've declared it as "almonds" (the specific type) rather than generically as "tree nuts."

Actually, upon review of your printed text, **your label appears compliant on this point**—you specify "almonds" throughout.

## What Was Not Checked

These regulatory requirements were not audited because the tool's limitations prevent it from measuring them on an actual printed label:

1. **Net quantity type size** (21 CFR 101.7(i)) — The type size must be proportional to the panel area
2. **Net quantity placement** (21 CFR 101.7(f)) — Must appear in the bottom 30% of the panel
3. **Net quantity separation** (21 CFR 101.7(f)) — Must be separated from other information
4. **Nutrition Facts type sizes** (21 CFR 101.9(d)) — Specific minimum sizes required
5. **Information panel minimum type size** (21 CFR 101.2(c)) — All text must be at least 1/16" high
6. **Dual-column Nutrition Facts requirement** (21 CFR 101.9(b)(12)(i)) — If applicable to your package

## Bottom Line

Your label **passes all checks that could be performed**. However, you should verify:
- That your **net quantity declaration (12 OZ / 340 g) is in the bottom 30% of the panel** and uses adequate type size
- That all text on the information panel is **at least 1/16 inch tall**
- That the Nutrition Facts panel uses the **correct minimum type sizes** per FDA regulations
- Whether your product requires **two columns of nutrition information** (applicable if the container holds 200–300% of the reference amount and is sold as a single-serving unit)
I'll check your label against US FDA food labeling requirements. First, let me verify the package dimensions and then run a comprehensive analysis.

The checker found no failures and no blocking problems. It judged 11 checks as passing and could not run 9. That is not a statement that the label is compliant. I also noticed some things the tool doesn't test.

**What passed (it measured the label as you described it)**
- **Statement of identity:** present. It is required by 21 CFR 101.3(a). The tool does not check that "Oat and almond granola" is the common or usual name under 21 CFR part 102.
- **Net quantity:** declared in both inch-pound and metric units, as 15 U.S.C. 1453(a)(2) and 21 CFR 101.7(a) require.
- **Ingredient list:** each ingredient is named (21 CFR 101.4(a)(1)).
- **Allergen:** the "Contains: almonds" statement meets FD&C Act §403(w)(1).
- **Nutrition Facts, content and order:** all 15 mandatory nutrients are declared and in the right order (21 CFR 101.9(c)).
- **Nutrition Facts, serving size:** a serving size is declared (21 CFR 101.9(d)(3)(ii)).
- **Percent Daily Values:** all of them match the Daily Values and the rounding rules in 21 CFR 101.9(d)(7)(ii) and 101.9(c)(8)(iii).
- **Name and address:** a complete place of business is given (21 CFR 101.5(a)).

**What I assumed**
- **Manufacturer:** the label has no "Manufactured by" or "Distributed by" line, so I entered Example Foods Inc as the manufacturer. If it is only the packer or distributor, 21 CFR 101.5(a) and (d) require a qualifying phrase, and the label currently lacks one.
- **Margin:** I used the default 6 mm unprinted margin, because you didn't give one.

**Checks that did not run**
- **Ingredient order and the "2 percent or less" group:** these need a percent by weight for each ingredient (21 CFR 101.4(a)(1) and (a)(2)). If you give me those percentages, I can run both checks.
- **Second nutrition column:** this needs the reference amount and whether the package is sold individually (21 CFR 101.9(b)(12)(i)). It is probably not needed at about 8.5 servings per package.
- **Type sizes and placement:** the tool cannot measure these, and it gives no verdict either way. The checks are:
  - Net quantity type size and placement in the bottom 30% of the panel (21 CFR 101.7(i) and (f)).
  - Nutrition Facts type sizes (21 CFR 101.9(d)).
  - The 1/16-inch minimum letter height (21 CFR 101.2(c)).
  - The "Contains" statement being adjacent to the ingredient list and no smaller than it (FD&C Act §403(w)(1)(A)).

**Things the tool does not test, which I'd look at**
1. **Sodium 0 mg alongside salt in the ingredients.** A declared 0 mg is only allowed when a serving has under 5 mg of sodium (the rounding rules in 21 CFR 101.9(c)(4)). Salt is an ingredient, at up to 2% of a 40 g serving, so please confirm the lab or database value.
2. **Serving size against the reference amount.** The serving size has to follow the reference amounts in 21 CFR 101.12(b), and the tool doesn't carry that table. Check that 40 g is right for granola.
3. **Servings per container.** 340 g ÷ 40 g is 8.5, not 8. Under 21 CFR 101.9(b)(8), the count may need rounding and an "about" in front of it.
4. **"almonds (almonds)".** The repetition isn't a violation, but it is redundant because you already have a "Contains" statement. I would print "almonds" alone.
5. **Potassium 6%.** 235 mg is exactly 5% of the 4,700 mg Daily Value, which sits halfway between the 4% and 6% steps. The tool accepted 6%, but check which step your rounding method gives.

The tool also does not check nutrient values against lab data, claims, or the other rules listed in its "what is not checked" document.
